what_it_is.prose: The Airbus C-295 is a twin-turboprop tactical transport aircraft being procured by the Indian Air Force to replace its legacy fleet of Avro HS-748 aircraft. The programme, signed on 24 September 2021 for ₹21,935 crore (~$2.5 billion), comprises 56 aircraft: 16 imported in fly-away condition from Airbus Defence and Space's Seville facility in Spain, and 40 assembled in India by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) at a dedicated Final Assembly Line (FAL) in Vadodara, Gujarat — the first private-sector military aircraft FAL in India. The Vadodara complex's foundation stone was laid in October 2022 and the facility was inaugurated on 28 October 2024 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Pre-FAL production began December 2024, FAL assembly commenced October 2025, and the first Make-in-India C-295 is scheduled to roll out in September 2026, with all 56 aircraft to be delivered by August 2031. All 16 imported aircraft had been delivered by August 2025. The C-295 has a payload of up to 9.5 tonnes and can carry up to 71 troops, 44–48 paratroopers or 24 stretchers, and is powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127G turboprops. Per the Government of India, indigenous content rises from 48% on the first 16 aircraft to 75% on the later India-built aircraft; of roughly 14,000 detail parts per aircraft, some 13,000 are made in India across 37 identified suppliers (33 of them MSMEs), and the electronic warfare suite is manufactured in India by Bharat Electronics Limited and Bharat Dynamics Limited. The programme is a landmark for Indian aerospace: the first time a private Indian company assembles a complete military transport aircraft under a Make-in-India model, with progressive indigenisation of airframe structures and sub-assemblies.

deployments_procurement.summary: India signed a ₹21,935 crore contract on 24 September 2021 for 56 C-295 aircraft (16 imported fly-away from Spain + 40 built by TASL at Vadodara). All 16 imported aircraft were delivered by August 2025. The Vadodara FAL was inaugurated on 28 October 2024; FAL assembly began October 2025 and the first India-built C-295 is scheduled to roll out in September 2026, with all deliveries complete by August 2031.

open_questions: Detailed delivery milestones for the 40 India-built C-295 between 2026 and 2031 are not publicly itemised.

import_dependencies.summary: The C-295 is a Spanish-origin Airbus design assembled in India with progressive indigenisation of the airframe (48% rising to 75%), but propulsion and several core systems remain imported.

items.note: Airbus Defence and Space (Spain) — fully imported design; India holds assembly and progressive build rights, not design authority.
Canada (P&WC) — no Indian production or alternative for the powerplant.
Airbus / Western avionics suppliers (Europe/USA); India integrates but does not own the baseline mission avionics.
Manufactured in India by Bharat Electronics Limited and Bharat Dynamics Limited — an indigenised element of the programme.

faq.question: Why is the C-295 programme significant for Indian aerospace manufacturing?
faq.answer: It is the first time a private Indian company (Tata Advanced Systems Limited) assembles a complete military aircraft. Of the 56 aircraft, 16 are imported fly-away from Airbus Seville and 40 are built at the Vadodara Final Assembly Line — the first private military aircraft FAL in India. Indigenous content rises from 48% on the first 16 to 75% on later India-built aircraft, with about 13,000 of 14,000 detail parts made in India across 37 suppliers (33 MSMEs), and the EW suite built by BEL and BDL.

faq.question: What is the C-295 replacing in IAF service?
faq.answer: The C-295 replaces the Indian Air Force's legacy Avro HS-748 transport fleet. It provides tactical airlift — troop and cargo transport, paradrop, logistics and casualty evacuation — with a payload of up to 9.5 tonnes and the ability to operate from unprepared runways, including Himalayan Advanced Landing Grounds.

faq.question: When will the first India-built C-295 be delivered?
faq.answer: All 16 imported aircraft were delivered by August 2025. FAL assembly of India-built aircraft began in October 2025 and the first Make-in-India C-295 is scheduled to roll out in September 2026, with all 56 aircraft to be delivered by August 2031. Detailed year-by-year milestones for the 40 India-built aircraft are not publicly itemised.
